issues.title: Refactor: Replace magic number '1388' (Small Business Yes) with named constant
issues.description:
## Summary
`onenlist.form.js` line 466 contains a hardcoded numeric value `"1388"` used to
represent the "Yes" lookup item for Small Business type. This magic number is
completely opaque — it is not documented, not tied to any named constant, and will
silently break if the lookup item ID changes in a different environment's database.
Similar hardcoded lookup IDs likely exist in other areas of the JavaScript and
C# code.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/wwwroot/scripts/onenlist.form.js:466`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The hardcoded value `"1388"` is replaced with a named data attribute rendered from the server (e.g., `data-sb-yes-id="@Model.SmallBusinessYesId"` on the relevant form element)
- [ ] The corresponding C# model/view exposes the lookup ID as a typed property, not a magic string
- [ ] A code search for other hardcoded lookup IDs in `.js`, `.cshtml`, and `.cs` files is performed; any found are similarly replaced with server-rendered data attributes
- [ ] The form continues to function correctly (Small Business checkbox mutual-exclusivity logic works)
- [ ] A code comment is added explaining the purpose of each data attribute (e.g., `// ID of the 'Yes' option in the Small Business lookup`)

issues.title: UX: Add help text and tooltips to Admin field configuration settings
issues.description:
## Summary
The Admin area field configuration (`FieldController`, `System_FieldMetadata`)
exposes settings like `IsRequired`, `IsHidden`, `ConditionallyRequired`, `IsFiltered`,
and `AllowDateNA`. These setting names are not self-explanatory — administrators
without deep domain knowledge cannot determine what `ConditionallyRequired` means,
what `IsFiltered` applies to (Service Code codes? dates?), or the downstream impact of toggling
`AllowDateNA`. There are no tooltips, inline help text, or documentation links in the
Admin UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each field configuration property in the Admin edit form has a help icon (ⓘ) with a Bootstrap tooltip or popover
- [ ] Tooltip content explains: what the setting does, what it affects in the end-user form, and any important side effects
- [ ] At minimum the following are documented: `IsRequired`, `IsHidden`, `ConditionallyRequired`, `IsFiltered`, `AllowDateNA`
- [ ] A link to the relevant GitLab wiki page (`unit-testing` or `user-guide`) is included at the top of the field configuration page
- [ ] Tooltips are keyboard-accessible (focusable via Tab, visible on focus)
- [ ] The existing field configuration CRUD functionality is unchanged

issues.title: UX: Improve API key management — add expiration display, usage count, and revocation log
issues.description:
## Summary
The Admin API key management screen (`ApiAccessKeysController`) shows the minimum
information needed to manage API keys but is missing critical operational visibility:
- No expiration date shown or enforced in the UI (keys never expire)
- No last-used timestamp or usage count
- No revocation history (can't tell when a key was revoked or by whom)
- No indication of which client/system is using each key

This makes it impossible for administrators to audit API access or identify stale/
compromised keys.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The API key list displays: Client ID, Issued Date, Expiration Date, Last Used Date (if tracked), Status (Active/Expired/Revoked)
- [ ] Administrators can set an expiration date when creating or editing a key
- [ ] Keys past their expiration date are automatically rejected by `ApiKeyAuthAttribute` with a clear error response
- [ ] A revocation log entry (timestamp, admin user, reason) is created when a key is revoked
- [ ] The revocation log is viewable from the key detail page
- [ ] An optional "Notes" field on each key allows documenting which system/integration uses it
- [ ] All existing API authentication tests continue to pass

issues.title: refactor: Switch action list data layer from stored procedures to EF IQueryable (Phase 2a follow-up to #675)
issues.description:
## Background

This is the deferred Phase 2a from #675. When that ticket added per-column filtering to the action list view, the original Phase 2a scope was to switch the list data layer from stored procedures (`GetOneNListItemsByStatus`, `GetOneNListItemsByRecentlyModified`, both wrapping `GetOneNListItemsByUser`) to EF `IQueryable<>` so structured filters would push to the SQL `WHERE` clause instead of running in-memory after the sproc returns.

A first attempt was made and **reverted** in commit `61f89ced` because the partial EF projection omitted ~110 of the SP's ~140 output fields plus the `CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt` aggregation, the `PEO_AdjudicationComments` STRING_AGG, and the default sort order. The reverted code is in commit `46683d31` for reference but is not on Development.

This ticket is a clean restart of that work, scoped as its own delivery so the per-field audit can be done carefully without competing with the user-visible filter UI features.

## Why now / why this matters

Today's flow:
1. SP returns full result set the user is allowed to see (could be 10k+ rows for the largest orgs)
2. C# applies text-search filter in-memory
3. C# applies column filters in-memory (added by #675 Phase 2b)
4. C# sorts in-memory
5. C# pages

Performance is acceptable today for orgs at ~3k rows but unproven at 10k+. The revert means structured filters added in #675 do not push to SQL — they run on the materialized result set just like the legacy text search does. As filterable columns proliferate per the org-configurable design, in-memory filtering will become the bottleneck before sort or paging does.

Switching the data layer to EF unlocks:
- Server-side WHERE pushdown for both text search and column filters
- Server-side paging via `Skip`/`Take` on the filtered set instead of after materializing the full set
- Server-side sorting via `OrderBy` chains
- Smaller wire footprint (only the page worth of rows leaves SQL)

## What needs to happen

### 1. Field-level audit (critical)

Before any C# changes, audit `GetOneNListItemsByUser` against every consumer in the codebase. Inventory all ~140 output fields and confirm each one's source on `OneNList` (or related tables). Capture as a markdown table in this ticket comment thread, columns:

| Result-class property | Source (OneNList column or join) | Consumed by |

Sources that need explicit handling:
- Direct `OneNList` columns → easy mapping
- Single-row LookupItem joins (e.g. `PMPD = LookupItem.LookupItemValue WHERE ID = fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID`) → 15+ of these
- POC_LookUp subqueries (`ACCBranchChiefName`, `ACCBranchChiefPhone`)
- `OneNList_ProjectedObligation` SUM aggregation (`CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt`) keyed on the current fiscal year (Oct–Sep)
- `OneNList_PEOAdjudicationComments` STRING_AGG (`PEO_AdjudicationComments`)
- `DateOnly?` → `DateTime?` conversion for ~25 date fields

### 2. Sibling SP review

`ListController` calls three SPs depending on context:
- `GetOneNListItemsByUser(userId, organizationId)` — base, only its source is in the original ticket attachment
- `GetOneNListItemsByStatus(userId, organizationId, statusId)` — used when `statusId > 1`
- `GetOneNListItemsByRecentlyModified(userId, organizationId)` — used for the "Recent" view

The other two SPs are NOT in the source-controlled migrations folder; their definitions exist only in the live database. Pull them out, diff against `GetOneNListItemsByUser`, document any status-view-specific filters or sort behavior so the EF query can replicate them.

### 3. Permission TVF integration

The TVF `dbo.fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor(userId, organizationId)` MUST remain the source of truth for permission scoping — its 5 access-level branches encode subtle Region/PM/LIMITED/Admin/Owner/Member/Visitor + Northline + Baymark + AllACC cross-access rules that would be a security bug to re-implement in C#.

The cleanest EF integration:
- Add a keyless EF type for the TVF result row (`PermittedOneNListId { int ID }`)
- Register as `HasNoKey()` in `OneNListContext`
- Project the TVF into a sub-`IQueryable` via `_dbContext.Set<PermittedOneNListId>().FromSqlInterpolated($"SELECT * FROM dbo.fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor({userId}, {organizationId})").Select(p => p.ID)`
- Compose the OneNList query as `_dbContext.Set<OneNList>().Where(o => permittedIds.Contains(o.ID))`

EF translates this to a `WHERE ID IN (SELECT ... FROM TVF)` subquery — identical predicate to the SP.

### 4. Service method signature

```csharp
// IOneNListItemService
IQueryable<GetOneNListItemsByUser> QueryForList(int userId, int organizationId, int? statusId);
```

Returns a composable `IQueryable<>` so `ListController` (or any future caller) can chain `.Where`, `.OrderBy`, `.Skip`, `.Take` and push everything to SQL.

### 5. ListController changes

Replace the SP fetch with `_itemService.QueryForList(...)`. Apply structured column filters via `ListFilterHelper.ApplyFilters(query, columnFilters, filterableColumns)` — this method already accepts `IQueryable<GetOneNListItemsByUser>` and chains `.Where` clauses; no changes needed. Apply text search via the same `.Where` predicate. Apply sort via `OrderBy` chains. Materialize the page only via `.Skip().Take().ToListAsync()`.

The `applyFilters` private method on `ListController` becomes obsolete and can be removed.

### 6. Default sort

`GetOneNListItemsByUser` ends with `ORDER BY I.CreatedDate DESC, I.ModifiedDate DESC`. The EF `QueryForList` must apply the equivalent default `OrderBy` when no explicit `sortOrder` is provided.

## Risks

- **Field omission causes silent data loss** — a missing field in the projection produces null/0 in the result, never an error. Caught only by manual UI testing or by a downstream consumer surprise. Mitigation: the audit table from step 1 is gated by code review.
- **CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt aggregation correctness** — fiscal-year boundary math (Oct = start of next FY) must match the SP's `CASE WHEN MONTH(GETDATE()) >= 10 THEN YEAR(GETDATE()) + 1 ELSE YEAR(GETDATE()) END`. Off-by-one errors here would misreport every action's funding total.
- **PEO_AdjudicationComments STRING_AGG** — EF Core's `string.Join` translation is limited; may need a `FromSqlInterpolated` projection or a computed column on `OneNList`.
- **Sibling SPs may have logic the base SP doesn't** — the audit in step 2 must capture this.
- **Test coverage is thin** — no existing tests assert on the SP result shape. Phase 3 of #675 added EF helper tests but not projection-completeness tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Field-level audit table posted as a comment on this ticket BEFORE any code changes; reviewed and signed off
- [ ] Source for sibling SPs (`GetOneNListItemsByStatus`, `GetOneNListItemsByRecentlyModified`) extracted from prod and posted in this ticket; logic differences from `GetOneNListItemsByUser` documented
- [ ] `IOneNListItemService.QueryForList(int userId, int organizationId, int? statusId)` returns `IQueryable<GetOneNListItemsByUser>` with EVERY field from the audit table populated
- [ ] Permission TVF integrated via keyless EF type; SQL trace confirms a single query with `WHERE ID IN (SELECT ... FROM TVF)` subquery
- [ ] Default `OrderBy(CreatedDate DESC).ThenByDescending(ModifiedDate DESC)` applied when no `sortOrder` is specified
- [ ] `CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt` aggregation matches the SP within ±$0.01 on a representative sample
- [ ] `PEO_AdjudicationComments` aggregation matches the SP byte-for-byte on a representative sample
- [ ] `ListController.Index` switched to `QueryForList` chain; legacy `applyFilters` private method deleted
- [ ] Page-level paging confirmed server-side (SQL trace shows `OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT`)
- [ ] Performance baseline captured BEFORE the cutover on a representative 10k+ row org (cold-cache and warm-cache page load)
- [ ] Performance baseline AFTER the cutover; warm-cache page load with no filters at most 110% of baseline; warm-cache page load with 3+ filters strictly faster than baseline
- [ ] All existing 351+ unit tests continue to pass
- [ ] New unit tests:
  - `OneNListItemService.QueryForList_AppliesPermissionTvf_ScopesRowsToUser`
  - `OneNListItemService.QueryForList_NoStatus_DoesNotRestrictByStatus`
  - `OneNListItemService.QueryForList_StatusGiven_RestrictsToThatStatus`
  - `OneNListItemService.QueryForList_DefaultSort_OrdersByCreatedDateDescending`
  - `OneNListItemService.QueryForList_PopulatesAllResultClassFields_FromAuditTable` (data-driven from the audit table)
- [ ] Manual UI smoke test against a non-prod environment: every column the list view renders shows the same value as the legacy SP path on a per-row diff of 100 representative rows
- [ ] Project builds with no errors and no new warnings
- [ ] Once shipped, the deferred AC from #675 ("server applies filters before paging; no regression > 20%") is met for #675 and that ticket can be closed-out

## Out of scope

- Changing the SP signature or removing the SPs from the database — they may still be called by other code paths (Excel exports, BI dashboards, audit logs). Inventory their other consumers before considering removal.
- The `BO_View_OneNList` view — separate concern, used by reporting.
- Any UI changes — purely a data-layer migration. The list view shouldn't notice the swap.

## Estimated effort

- Field audit: 0.5 sprint
- Sibling SP extraction + diff: 0.5 sprint
- Implementation + tests: 1 sprint
- Manual UI verification + perf baselining: 0.5 sprint

**Total: ~2.5 sprints.** Recommend splitting if the team wants smaller increments.

issues.title: Add OrbitalLink checkbox to Action Description (alongside FieldSat field)
issues.description:
## Customer request
> "Add a checkbox for OrbitalLink… I would like to have that added where the FieldSat field is."

Add a new boolean **OrbitalLink** checkbox to the Action Description section of the item/action form, positioned next to the existing **FieldSat** checkbox.

## Approach
This is a direct mirror of the recently-added **FieldSat Action** field (`IsmVSATAction`, ticket #711, migrations in `Source/Migrations/5.1.3/`). Replicate that exact pattern for a new `IsStarshieldAction` (`bit`, NOT NULL, default 0) field. No new architecture is required.

## Implementation checklist (mirror of #711)
1. **Entity** — add `public bool? IsStarshieldAction { get; set; }` to `Source/OneNListApp.Data/Models/OneNList.cs` (next to `IsmVSATAction`, ~line 161). No explicit Fluent config needed (name convention).
2. **Migration (new version folder, e.g. `Source/Migrations/5.1.4/`)**:
   - `ALTER TABLE [dbo].[OneNList] ADD [IsStarshieldAction] BIT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_OneNList_IsStarshieldAction DEFAULT 0;`
   - `ALTER PROCEDURE [dbo].[UpdateActionDescriptionSection]` — add `@IsStarshieldAction bit = 0` param and `,[IsStarshieldAction] = @IsStarshieldAction` in the UPDATE SET (pattern: `01_20260508_AddIsmVSATActionField.sql`).
   - Add `[IsStarshieldAction]` to the `BO_View_OneNList` SELECT (pattern: `02_20260508_AddIsmVSATActionToBO_OneNList.sql`).
   - Seed `System_FieldMetadata` rows per organization (`ContainerTypeName='ActionDescription|System.Boolean'`, `FieldName='IsStarshieldAction'`, `DisplayName='OrbitalLink'`). **Decide default per-org visibility** — #711 set `IsHidden=0` for org 1 (Vantage North/Vantage) and `IsHidden=1` for orgs 2/3/4; confirm with the customer which org(s) should see OrbitalLink.
3. **Service** — add `bool? IsStarshieldAction` param to `UpdateActionDescriptionSection` in `Source/OneNListApp.Service/IStoredProcedureService.cs` and `StoredProcedureService.cs` (pass `@IsStarshieldAction = {IsStarshieldAction}`).
4. **ViewModel** — `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Models/ItemActionDescriptionViewModel.cs`: add `[Display(Name="OrbitalLink")] [FieldMetadata(AllowDuplicate=false, AllowHidden=true)] public bool IsStarshieldAction { get; set; }` plus `hdIsStarshieldAction`; map it in both `SetSectionValues` and `GetSectionValues`.
5. **View** — `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/Item/_ItemActionDescriptionSection.cshtml`: add a `BeginHalfSectionFor` + `CustomCheckBoxFor` block **immediately adjacent to the FieldSat block (~lines 84-95)**, plus the `HiddenFor` line. (Customer explicitly wants it "where the FieldSat field is.")
6. **Update helper** — `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/OneNItemUpdateHelper.cs`: pass `viewModel.ItemActionDescriptionSection.IsStarshieldAction` into the `UpdateActionDescriptionSection` call.
7. **Tests** — `Source/OneNListApp.Tests/Web/OneNItemUpdateHelperTests.cs`: add true/false persistence tests mirroring the `IsmVSATAction` tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- A "OrbitalLink" checkbox appears beside the FieldSat checkbox in the Action Description section, for the organization(s) the customer specifies.
- Its value persists on create/edit and round-trips correctly (verified by unit tests).
- It honors read-only mode and per-org hide/show via `System_FieldMetadata`, exactly like FieldSat.
- It is **not** copied when duplicating an action (`AllowDuplicate=false`), matching FieldSat.

## Open question
- Which organization(s) should have OrbitalLink visible by default? (FieldSat defaulted to visible for org 1 only.)

## Rough effort
S–M (well-trodden pattern; ~1 day incl. migration + tests).

_Source: lookup/codebase review; mirrors ticket #711 (FieldSat)._

issues.title: fix: Type of Submission required asterisk persists after admin sets field to not-required (and required validation blocks save)
issues.description:
## Summary
Reported by PMs (customer-direct). On the Item action **create/edit** screen, the **Type of Submission** field has two related defects:

1. **Required validation blocked saving** the action even though a Type of Submission selection could not be registered. PMs could not move forward to save.
2. **After an admin unchecked "Required"** in Admin field configuration, the action saves, **but the red required asterisk still shows**, which confuses PMs.

## Root cause analysis
`Type of Submission` is rendered as a checkbox list in `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/Item/_ItemActionDescriptionSection.cshtml` and is bound to a `SelectMultipleViewModel` (`ItemActionDescriptionViewModel`).

**Asterisk persists (symptom 2):** The required asterisk (CSS `is-required` class) is driven by `ModelMetadata.AdditionalValues["IsRequired"]`, which `FieldMetadataProvider` populates **once** and which ASP.NET Core caches for the application lifetime. `HtmlSectionHelpers` / the label helpers read this stale cached value, so toggling "Required" off in the DB field config is **not reflected until the app restarts** — the asterisk keeps rendering.

**Required validation vs. checkbox (symptom 1):** When the field is configured Required, `FieldMetadataProvider` adds a `RequiredAttribute`, and the empty-state check in `OneNItemValidationHelper` evaluates the object / `value.ToString()` rather than the underlying `SelectMultipleViewModel.Ids` collection. Because the view model object is never null, the "empty" detection is inconsistent with how the field is actually selected, contributing to the inability to satisfy the requirement.

## Files to investigate / modify
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/FieldMetadataProvider.cs` — make the `IsRequired` (and related display) flag reflect the **current** field metadata, or invalidate the metadata cache when Admin field config changes, so the asterisk tracks the live config.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/HtmlSectionHelpers.cs` and `HtmModelMetadatalHelpers.cs` — ensure the asterisk (`is-required`) reads the same live `IsRequired` value that drives validation.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/OneNItemValidationHelper.cs` — correctly evaluate "empty" for `SelectMultipleViewModel` fields (i.e. `Ids == null || Ids.Length == 0`).
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/Item/_ItemActionDescriptionSection.cshtml` — confirm the checkbox list renders and is enabled when options are present (verify `TypeOfSubmissionList` is populated).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Setting **Required = off** for Type of Submission in Admin field config removes the red asterisk on the next page load — no application restart required.
- [ ] When Required = on, the asterisk shows **and** save is blocked only when no Type of Submission is selected; selecting a value allows the action to save.
- [ ] A user can check a Type of Submission checkbox and successfully save the action.
- [ ] The asterisk display and required-enforcement always agree — no state where the asterisk shows but the field is not enforced, or vice versa.
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements
- `OneNItemValidationHelper.<method>_SelectMultipleRequiredAndEmpty_ReturnsRequiredError`
- `OneNItemValidationHelper.<method>_SelectMultipleRequiredWithSelection_Passes`
- Metadata/asterisk: required flag reflects an updated (toggled-off) field configuration rather than a cached value.

issues.title: fix: Home page funded amounts only show current FY (FY26) — show FY27 and future fiscal years
issues.description:
## Summary
Reported by PMs (customer-direct). On the PULSE home/action-list page, **funded amounts only show FY26**. FY27 collection has begun and those amounts need to display as well.

## Root cause analysis
The home/action list surfaces a **single computed "current fiscal year"** value rather than iterating all fiscal years that have data.

In `Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListItemService.cs` the current FY is computed once:
```csharp
var today = DateTime.Now;
int currentFy = today.Month >= 10 ? today.Year + 1 : today.Year;
```
and `CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt` only sums rows where `ObligationYear == currentFy`:
```csharp
CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt = ... Where(p => p.fk_OneNList_ID == o.ID && p.ObligationYear == currentFy).Sum(p => p.Amount) ...
```
As of June 2026, `currentFy == 2026`, so only FY26 shows; FY27 data (`ObligationYear == 2027`) is filtered out until the calendar rolls to October. The value is surfaced as the **"Current FY Obligation Amount"** column in `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml` (model property `CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt` on `GetOneNListItemsByUser`).

> Note for implementer: confirm with the requester whether the desired display is the existing "Current FY Obligation Amount" column or a separate funded-amount summary. The fix below assumes the FY-bound aggregation above is the source.

## Files to investigate / modify
- `Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListItemService.cs` — replace the single hardcoded `currentFy` aggregation with a per-fiscal-year aggregation covering all FYs that have data (at minimum FY26 and FY27, growing automatically).
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/StoredProcedures/Models/GetOneNListItemsByUser.cs` — expose funded amounts per fiscal year (or a collection keyed by FY) rather than a single `CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt`.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml` — render funded amounts for each relevant fiscal year instead of the single current-FY column.
- If a stored procedure backs the column, update the corresponding SQL under `Source/Migrations/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Funded amounts display for every fiscal year that has data — at minimum FY26 **and** FY27.
- [ ] New fiscal years appear automatically as data is collected, with no hardcoded single FY.
- [ ] Existing FY26 totals are unchanged.
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements
- `OneNListItemService.<method>_MultipleFiscalYears_ReturnsAmountPerFiscalYear`
- `OneNListItemService.<method>_Fy27DataPresent_IncludesFy27Total`

issues.title: feat: Add newly created LOE values to the Level of Effort lookup
issues.description:
## Summary
Reported by PMs (customer-direct). New **LOE (Level of Effort)** values were created for new funding and actions and need to be added so they appear in the LOE dropdown on the action description form.

## Background / how LOE works
LOE is a **database lookup**, not an enum:
- Stored as `LookupItem` rows under the `LevelOfEffort` lookup (`Enumerations.eLookups.LevelOfEffort`).
- Populated for the dropdown via `_sprocService.GetLookupItemsFor((int)Enumerations.eLookups.LevelOfEffort, organizationId)` in `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ItemController.cs`.
- Bound to `OneNList.fk_LevelOfEffort_Lookup_ID` and rendered in `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/Item/_ItemActionDescriptionSection.cshtml` (ViewData key `LevelOfEffortDropDownList`).
- LOE has special handling for an optional `LookupItemNumericValue` ("LOE_ID") in the Admin Lookup Item edit screen.

## How to add values
Two paths:
1. **SQL migration (preferred for a coordinated release):** add a new file under `Source/Migrations/5.1.4/` following the `NN_YYYYMMDD_Description.sql` convention, with **idempotent** INSERTs into `LookupItem` (`fk_Lookup_ID` = LevelOfEffort) plus matching `Organization_Lookup_Config` rows so the values display for the correct organization(s).
2. **Admin UI:** an Owner-level user adds values via Admin > Lookup Items > Create for Lookup (LevelOfEffort).

## ⚠ Blocked — input required from requester
This ticket cannot be implemented until the requester provides:
- [ ] The exact new LOE value name(s).
- [ ] Optional LOE_ID (`LookupItemNumericValue`) for each, if applicable.
- [ ] Which organization(s) should see each new value.

## Files to modify
- `Source/Migrations/5.1.4/0N_YYYYMMDD_AddLevelOfEffortValues.sql` (new) — idempotent inserts into `LookupItem` and `Organization_Lookup_Config` for the LevelOfEffort lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The new LOE value(s) appear in the Level of Effort dropdown on the action description form for the specified organization(s).
- [ ] Existing LOE values and any actions already referencing them are unchanged.
- [ ] The migration is idempotent (re-running does not create duplicates).
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

issues.title: Add Excel import tool for LevelOfEffort lookup items (Action Descriptions)
issues.description:
## Summary

Add a self-service **"Import from Excel"** tool to the **Level of Effort (LOE)** lookup, surfaced inside the **Lookup Settings** section of the Section Field Metadata Settings page:

`/Admin/Field/Edit?Id=LevelOfEffort&Section=ItemActionDescription&Src=...`

Today the monthly LOE refresh is done by hand-writing `UPDATE`/`INSERT` statements against `[OneNList].[dbo].[LookupItem]` from a vendor-supplied Excel file. This ticket replaces that manual process with an in-app uploader that validates the file, previews the changes, and on confirmation updates existing LOEs and adds new ones in a single transaction.

The feature is **scoped to the LevelOfEffort lookup only** — the import UI must not appear for any other lookup.

---

## Background / Architecture (verified against the codebase)

- **Page/controller:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/FieldController.cs` → `Edit()` (GET, reads `Id`/`Section` from `Request.Query`). View: `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Views/Field/Edit.cshtml`. The **Lookup Settings** table is rendered inline in `Edit.cshtml` (~lines 170–243), driven by `FieldViewModel.Lookup` and `FieldViewModel.LookupConfigs` (`Organization_Lookup_Config[]`).

## Column / data mapping (Excel → `[dbo].[LookupItem]`)

| LookupItem column        | Source (Excel)            | Rule |
|--------------------------|---------------------------|------|
| `ID`                     | —                         | Unchanged for existing; let SQL identity assign for new rows |
| `fk_Lookup_ID`           | from `[dbo].[Lookup]`     | Resolve via `LookupService.GetByNameAsync("LevelOfEffort")` |
| `LookupItemValue`        | `LevelOfEffortName`       | Set/overwrite for both new and existing (≤150 chars) |
| `parentId`               | —                         | `NULL` |
| `CreatedBy`              | —                         | Unchanged for existing; new = `SessionManager.GetUserName()` |
| `CreatedDate`            | —                         | Unchanged for existing; new = current date/time |
| `ModifiedBy`             | —                         | Current logged-in username (always) |
| `ModifiedDate`           | —                         | Current date/time (always) |
| `LookupItemNumericValue` | `LevelOfEffortId`         | **Match key** (see below); set for new rows |

**Match key:** an LOE is "existing" when a `LookupItem` with `fk_Lookup_ID = <LevelOfEffort>` has `LookupItemNumericValue == LevelOfEffortId` from the file. Match → update `LookupItemValue`, `ModifiedBy`, `ModifiedDate`. No match → insert new `LookupItem`.

**Excel columns ignored** (present in vendor file but unused): `LevelOfEffortShortName`, `OrganizationalElementShortName`, `HasActiveFunding`.

## Required behavior (decisions confirmed with product owner)

1. **New LOEs mirror the manual "Create New Lookup Item" flow.** After inserting the `LookupItem`, also create an `Organization_Lookup_Config` for the **current organization** (`fk_Organization_ID = GetOrganizationId()`, `fk_Lookup_ID = <LevelOfEffort>`, `fk_LookupItem_ID = new id`, `IsActive = true`, `DisplayOrder` appended to the end of the current org's existing LOE configs — i.e. `max(DisplayOrder)+1`, not the hardcoded `1` used by the single-item create path). If a matched **existing** LOE has no config row for the current org, create one (active) too.
2. **Preview → Confirm (two-step).** Upload parses + validates server-side and returns a **preview** showing counts and itemized lists: *N to update*, *M to add*, *K to deactivate*, plus any warnings. The user clicks **Confirm** to commit. Nothing is written to the DB until Confirm. Avoid storing the uploaded file server-side between requests — return the validated rows serialized (e.g. JSON in a hidden field, with antiforgery) and have the Confirm POST deserialize and apply. (`TempData` is an acceptable alternative if simpler.)
3. **Deactivate LOEs missing from the file.** Any LOE currently configured/active for the **current organization** whose `LookupItemNumericValue` is **not** present in the uploaded file → set its `Organization_Lookup_Config.IsActive = false` (the file becomes the source of truth for what is active in this org). Do **not** delete `LookupItem` rows and do **not** modify their `LookupItemValue`. List these in the preview so the admin sees exactly what will be deactivated.
4. **Reject the whole file on any precheck failure.** Commit nothing; show a clear, itemized list of every problem so the admin can fix the source file and re-upload. Precheck must verify:
   - Required headers present (case-insensitive, trimmed): **`LevelOfEffortId`** and **`LevelOfEffortName`**. (Tolerate the ignored optional columns being present or absent.)
   - At least one data row.
   - Each row: `LevelOfEffortId` non-blank and a valid integer; `LevelOfEffortName` non-blank and ≤150 chars.
   - `LevelOfEffortId` values are **unique** within the file (report duplicates).
5. **All-or-nothing commit.** Wrap the apply step in a single DB transaction (`OneNListContext.Database.BeginTransactionAsync()` or service-level equivalent) so a mid-batch failure rolls everything back.
6. **Scope/visibility:** render the "Import from Excel" affordance only when `Model.Lookup?.Name == "LevelOfEffort"`. Reuse the area's existing admin authorization (same as the rest of `FieldController`/`LookupItemController`); no new auth scheme.

## Proposed implementation outline

**Service layer (`OneNListApp.Service`)**
- New `ILevelOfEffortImportService` / `LevelOfEffortImportService`:
  - `ParseAndValidate(IFormFile file)` → returns a result object with: `IsValid`, `Errors` (list), and a list of validated row DTOs (`LevelOfEffortId`, `LevelOfEffortName`).
  - `BuildPreviewAsync(IReadOnlyList<LoeRowDto> rows, int organizationId)` → diff against current DB/org state → `{ ToUpdate[], ToAdd[], ToDeactivate[], Warnings[] }`.
  - `ApplyAsync(IReadOnlyList<LoeRowDto> rows, int organizationId, string username, DateTime now)` → performs update/insert/deactivate inside one transaction; returns a summary (counts).
  - DTO `LoeRowDto { int LevelOfEffortId; string LevelOfEffortName; }`.
  - Register in `Program.cs` next to the other lookup services.
- Reuse the ClosedXML parsing approach from `BulkUploadService` (first worksheet, header row = row 1, data from row 2).

**Controller (`Areas/Admin/Controllers/FieldController.cs`)**
- `[HttpPost] PreviewLevelOfEffortImport(IFormFile file)` → validate `.xlsx`; call `ParseAndValidate`; if invalid return the preview/error partial with the error list; if valid call `BuildPreviewAsync` and return the preview partial (modal) including the serialized validated rows + antiforgery token.
- `[HttpPost][ValidateAntiForgeryToken] ApplyLevelOfEffortImport(<serialized rows>)` → deserialize, re-resolve org/user from `SessionManager`, call `ApplyAsync`, return `Json(new { success = true, reloadPage = true })` (consistent with existing lookup modals). On failure set `SessionManager.ErrorMessage` / return the partial with errors.

**View (`Areas/Admin/Views/Field/Edit.cshtml` + new partials)**
- In the Lookup Settings section, add an **"Import from Excel"** link (icon + label, same styling as "Create New Lookup Item"/"Edit Lookup Settings"), rendered only for the LevelOfEffort lookup, opening an AJAX modal.
- Modal partial: file input (`.xlsx`) + Upload button → posts to `PreviewLevelOfEffortImport`.
- Preview partial: summary counts + three lists (Update / Add / Deactivate) + warnings/errors; **Confirm** and **Cancel** buttons. Confirm posts to `ApplyLevelOfEffortImport`. On success the modal triggers the existing page reload so the refreshed table renders.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the LevelOfEffort field edit page, an "Import from Excel" control appears in Lookup Settings; it does **not** appear for any other lookup.
- [ ] Uploading a valid `.xlsx` shows a preview listing exactly which LOEs will be updated, added, and deactivated, with counts — **no DB changes yet**.
- [ ] Confirming applies all changes in one transaction: existing LOEs (matched by `LookupItemNumericValue` = `LevelOfEffortId`) have `LookupItemValue`, `ModifiedBy`, `ModifiedDate` updated; new LOEs are inserted with `fk_Lookup_ID` resolved by name, `parentId = NULL`, audit fields set, and an active `Organization_Lookup_Config` (display order appended) for the current org.
- [ ] LOEs active for the current org but absent from the file are deactivated (config `IsActive = false`); their `LookupItem` rows and names are untouched.
- [ ] A file missing `LevelOfEffortId`/`LevelOfEffortName` headers, with no data rows, with blank/non-numeric ids, blank/over-length names, or duplicate ids is **rejected with an itemized error list and zero DB writes**.
- [ ] `fk_Lookup_ID` is resolved via `LookupService.GetByNameAsync("LevelOfEffort")` (no hardcoded id).
- [ ] The Service layer has no dependency on `SessionManager` (user/org/timestamp passed in).
- [ ] Unit tests (written test-first, PULSE convention) cover: header validation, missing data, non-numeric/blank/duplicate id, over-length name, update-existing, add-new (incl. config creation + display-order append), and deactivate-missing diff logic.
